title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page fixes the normalisation constant that compares two Gysin (push-forward) maps for a closed immersion Y ⊂ X of complex manifolds or smooth varieties of codimension p. One map is the topological Gysin map P_top, defined on Betti cohomology with Z or C coefficients. The other is the analytic (de Rham) Gysin map P_an, defined on hypercohomology of the holomorphic de Rham complexes Ω^•_Y → Ω^•_X.

Step 1, local computation in codimension 1. Take X a disc with coordinate z and Y = {a} = {z = 0}.
- Via the residue / boundary description, P_an(1_Y) corresponds to the class on X − a of the form dz/z. The marginal note says to write out this argument ('faire le raisonnement').
- Both maps land in the rank-one group H^2_Y(X) ≅ H^1(X − a), so P_an(1_Y) = λ·P_top(1_Y). The topological class is normalised to integrate to 1 on a small counter-clockwise circle C.
- Hence λ = ∫_C dz/z = 2πi, so P_top(1_Y) = (1/2πi)·P_an(1_Y) and P_an(1_Y) = 2πi·P_top(1_Y).
- A first attempt, written as P_an((1/2πi)1_Y) = P_top(1_Y), is crossed out and replaced by these two boxed formulas.

Step 2, globalisation (labelled 'Cor', i.e. corollary). Consider the diagram with rows
- top: H^{i+p}(X,Z) → H^{i+p}(X,C) ≅ (de Rham) H^{i+p}(X,Ω^•_X),
- bottom: H^i(Y,Z) → H^i(Y,C) → H^i(Y,Ω^•_Y),
and vertical maps P_top, P_top, P_an.

The diagram commutes provided the bottom comparison isomorphism is taken to be (2πi)^{-p} times the canonical de Rham isomorphism. Equivalently, for every class c, P_an(DR_Y c) = (2πi)^p · DR_X(P_top c). This extends the local formula to arbitrary codimension p, to global X, and to arbitrary cohomology classes on Y in place of 1_Y.

Purpose: the integrality of algebraic cycle classes and the Tate twist Z(1) = 2πi·Z in the motives / Hodge-theory programme. These are the compatibilities needed to make Betti, de Rham and Hodge realisations of motives agree. The surrounding pages in the folder are unrelated typed Bourbaki/Lazard drafts on formal groups (n° 413) used as scrap paper.
errors: No mathematical error. Signs depend on orientation conventions (counter-clockwise circle, residue sign), which the page fixes explicitly.
The bottom isomorphism must indeed be (2πi)^{-p}·can for commutativity given P_an = (2πi)^p P_top. This is consistent with the boxed formulas.
The general-codimension statement is asserted, not proved. Reduction to codimension 1 (via deformation to the normal bundle, or blow-up / products of divisors) is left implicit.

ideas.what: Comparison of analytic (de Rham) and topological cycle classes / Gysin maps differs by a factor (2πi)^p in codimension p, computed via ∫ dz/z = 2πi
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of Betti and de Rham cycle class maps up to (2πi)^p; Tate twist Z(p) = (2πi)^p Z
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties, 1966, remarks on 2πi); Deligne (Théorie de Hodge II, 1971; Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, 1982); Atiyah–Hodge; standard in Hartshorne's and El Zein's work on the de Rham fundamental class
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties', Publ. IHES 29 (1966) (2πi normalisation of Chern / cycle classes); also implicit in SGA 4½-era / Deligne treatments

ideas.what: Commutative diagram relating Gysin maps on Z-, C- and de Rham cohomology with twisted comparison isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: Gysin morphism compatible with comparison isomorphism (Betti–de Rham realisation of the Tate motive)

deep.surprise_reason: A standard normalisation computation (the 2πi factor between topological and de Rham Gysin maps), well known and published by Grothendieck and Deligne. It is of interest only as a record of Grothendieck working out the Tate-twist bookkeeping for motives / Hodge realisations.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 'comme si P_an(1_Y) = λ P_top(1_Y)' is better read as 'par suite comme [on sait que / on a] P_an(1_Y) = λ P_top(1_Y)'.
In the diagram the top-middle and bottom-middle groups are H^{i+p}(X,C) and H^i(Y,C); the asterisk-like symbols and subscripts are overwritten or crossed out.
The right column is hypercohomology of the de Rham complex Ω^•_X (resp. Ω^•_Y).
The crossed-out word above the bottom isomorphism is 'Rel' (or similar), replaced by '~' with the label '1/(2iπ)^p can.'
The label under the first integral reads 'cercle anticlock[wise] orienté', with 'clock' crossed out.
